title: Relegation Panic: Abia dissolves Enyimba management, technical crew
summary: Abia has dissolved Enyimba’s management and technical staff as the club sits 18th after 13 matches. The state says reforms will address operational problems.
body:
The Abia State Government has dissolved the management structure and technical crew of Enyimba International Football Club with immediate effect, as the club struggles near the bottom of the Nigeria Premier Football League. Enyimba are 18th after 13 matches in the 2026/27 season, with three wins, two draws and eight defeats. Their latest loss was a 1-0 home defeat to Ikorodu City on Sunday, leaving them on 11 points.

In a statement signed by Commissioner for Information Okey Kanu, the government said it had identified administrative and structural problems contributing to the club’s poor performance. It said broad intervention was needed to address issues affecting Enyimba’s results, administration and operations.

The Ministry of Sports and Youth Development has been directed to lead the restructuring, review the club’s management framework and carry out administrative, technical, operational and institutional reforms. Management and technical personnel affected by the decision, along with anyone holding club assets, property, official documents or equipment, have been told to hand them over to the ministry. Further information on the handover and administrative process is expected from the ministry. People within the club say former Super Eagles captain Nwankwo Kanu may remain chairman, although the government’s announcement did not confirm his position.

The intervention follows a period of instability at the club, including frequent coaching changes. Enyimba had four coaches across 29 league matches in the previous campaign. Concerns have also been raised about recruitment, player welfare and administrative continuity. The club’s most recent league title came in the 2023/24 season under Finidi George. Enyimba have won the CAF Champions League twice, in 2003 and 2004. The state government described the club as part of Abia’s sporting heritage and said the restructuring aims to strengthen its institutions, improve accountability and restore its competitive standing. Its immediate task is to move clear of the relegation zone.

title: Top 10 most affordable states to live in Nigeria in October 2026
summary: Taraba recorded Nigeria’s lowest annual headline inflation in October 2026, as national inflation eased to 14.06%. The ranking measures price growth, not absolute living costs.
body:
Taraba had the lowest annual headline inflation rate among Nigerian states in October 2026, at 6.1%, followed by Sokoto at 6.7% and Ekiti at 7.6%. All ten states in the ranking were below the national rate of 14.06%, which fell from 14.63% in September, according to the National Bureau of Statistics’ October consumer price report. National food inflation also eased, to 19.13% from 19.59%.

The remaining states in the top ten were Ogun at 8.5%, Oyo at 8.8%, Osun and Katsina at 9.3%, Jigawa and Ondo at 10.3%, and Cross River at 11.2%. The state-level ranking shifted from September: Taraba retained the top spot, while Bauchi and Adamawa, previously among the three lowest, dropped out of the top ten. The South-West accounted for the largest share of October’s list; no North-Central or South-East state featured.

The figures also show that lower headline inflation did not always mean lower food inflation. Ondo’s food inflation was 31.7%, the highest among the ten states, while Oyo’s was 28.8%. Sokoto’s food inflation rose to 21.4% from 6.1% in September, even as its headline rate fell to 6.7% from 8.0%. Taraba’s food inflation rose from -7.5% to 8.9%, remaining below the national food rate. By contrast, Cross River’s food inflation declined to 16.3% from 21.2%.

The report describes differences in agricultural production, food-market access, transport and distribution networks, and state interventions as factors associated with local price trends. The ranking compares the annual rate of price increases; it does not establish which states have the lowest overall cost of living. Lagos, for example, recorded headline inflation of 15.5% and food inflation of 31.4%, placing 24th nationally.

title: South Africa cautions Fani-Kayode over social media remarks
summary: South Africa cautioned Nigerian High Commissioner Femi Fani-Kayode over social media comments after a dispute about his speech at a credentials ceremony.
body:
South Africa has conveyed its concerns to Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, over events following the presentation of his diplomatic credentials and his subsequent social media remarks. The Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) said the concerns were raised during a meeting on Tuesday between its Director-General, Zane Dangor, and Fani-Kayode.

Dangor referred to Article 41 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which requires diplomatic agents to conduct official business with the receiving state through its foreign ministry. DIRCO said the meeting emphasised that official communications should use established diplomatic channels, including the department.

The dispute began after Fani-Kayode presented his Letters of Credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa at the Sefako Makgatho Presidential Guest House in Pretoria on November 13, alongside ambassadors from 14 other countries. Fani-Kayode alleged that the official livestream excluded his introduction and speech, saying it cut away when he was due to speak and resumed after his address. The South African Presidency later published a separate video of his speech.

Ramaphosa’s spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, disputed Fani-Kayode’s account of the president’s response to his complaint. Magwenya said Ramaphosa had directed him to the appropriate officials and had no mandate to interfere in the South African Broadcasting Corporation’s operations or editorial decisions. The exchange prompted a public response from the Nigerian High Commission, which defended the envoy and called for restraint and resolution through diplomatic channels. The SABC said Fani-Kayode declined an interview invitation over the handling of the livestream, while remaining open to engagement with him and the mission.

DIRCO said South Africa remained committed to strengthening its strategic partnership with Nigeria and maintaining constructive engagement based on mutual respect and cooperation. The meeting marks a further effort to address the disagreement while preserving relations between the two countries.

title: Flamingos captain plans outreach after World Cup triumph
summary: Flamingos captain Harmony Chidi plans an outreach for people in need after Nigeria’s U-17 World Cup win. She has previously visited patients in Owerri.
body:
Nigeria captain Harmony Chidi says she plans to launch an outreach initiative to help people facing difficult circumstances, using part of the rewards promised to the Flamingos after their World Cup victory. The 17-year-old said she would share details of her plans soon. She previously visited pregnant women and sick patients at a hospital in Owerri, Imo State, in July, and has said she tries to help others with what she has.

Chidi led Nigeria to a 2-1 win over Japan in the final on November 7, securing the country’s first FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup title and making Nigeria the first African nation to win the tournament. The team’s achievement was followed by several announced rewards. President Bola Tinubu approved a five-year Federal Government Savings Bond of ₦100m for each player, to be held until they turn 18. Head coach Akeem Busari was awarded N100m in cash, while technical crew members were allocated N50m each.

The Senate pledged N100m to the team. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu announced N10m for each player and coaching crew member, along with iPhone 17 Pro Max devices and other gifts.

Chidi has described overcoming family and career challenges on her path to the title. After her father died early, her mother opposed her football ambition, while her grandmother encouraged her to continue until her death. Chidi has also credited her foster father, Prince Chidi, who owns her grassroots team, Imo Strikers, with supporting her ambitions. A serious injury had ruled her out of the previous tournament, but she recovered to captain Nigeria to victory in Morocco.

title: War on terror: Over 2,000 suspected terrorists facing prosecution — Tinubu
summary: Tinubu says more than 2,000 suspected terrorists are facing prosecution and over 1,000 have been convicted. He also reports four senior leaders killed or arrested.
body:
Tinubu says more than 2,000 suspected terrorists are facing prosecution and more than 1,000 have been convicted, as Nigerian security forces intensify operations against armed groups. He said the country had killed or arrested four of eight identified senior terrorist leaders. The president’s remarks were delivered by National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu at the opening of the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja.

Tinubu cited the elimination of senior Islamic State leader Abu Bilal al-Minuki in May 2026 and the arrests of Abu Barra of Ansaru and Mamuda of Mahmudawa in 2025 among the reported gains. He also referred to action against Ahmed Ohida’s ISWAP southern expansion network. The four leaders still being pursued, he said, are Ba Shuwa of ISWAP, Abdullahi Oro of IS-Sahel, Sadiku of JAS in the North Central region and Bakura Doro in the Lake Chad Basin. Tinubu added that security forces had killed senior bandit leader Halilu Sububu and other fighters.

The president said the government aims to turn operational gains into lasting security through intelligence-sharing and coordinated work among security agencies. He called for greater use of artificial intelligence, geospatial intelligence and unmanned surveillance, while stressing that AI-generated analysis requires human verification and that data protection and cybersecurity must be built into systems. He also said he had directed the preparation of a national threat assessment and a five-year strategic defence operations plan.

Tinubu reported that incidents of illegal oil bunkering and damage to oil and gas infrastructure in the Niger Delta fell from 32 in the first quarter of 2026 to 17 in the third, a reduction of 46.88 per cent. He said crude oil and condensate production averaged about 1.68 million barrels per day in August 2026. Defence Minister Christopher Musa emphasised the importance of timely intelligence and indigenous defence production, while Chief of Defence Staff Olufemi Oluyede called for more investment in intelligence technology and proactive operations.

title: Shettima announces presidential directive on immediate fertiliser supply for dry season farming
summary: Shettima ordered agencies and fertiliser firms to expedite supplies of more than three million bags for dry-season farming. The initiative targets affordability and local production.
body:
Vice President Kashim Shettima has directed government agencies and fertiliser industry stakeholders to accelerate production and distribution of more than three million bags of fertiliser ahead of the coming dry-season farming period. The directive followed President Bola Tinubu’s approval of funding under the Renewed Hope Agricultural Stabilisation and Productivity Initiative, which is intended to make fertiliser more affordable and support domestic production. Shettima gave the instruction at a meeting with industry stakeholders at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

He directed the Office of the National Security Adviser to verify and monitor stocks declared by stakeholders, with the stated aim of ensuring transparent accounting and an orderly distribution process. He also called for farmers in states facing security challenges, including those in vulnerable or hard-to-reach communities, to be included. Under the initiative, the federal government plans to buy fertiliser made by Nigerian blending companies and make it available to farmers at affordable prices.

The Fertiliser Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria said available raw materials could support production of about 148,000 metric tonnes of NPK 20-10-10 fertiliser in the coming weeks, equivalent to roughly three million bags. FEPSAN president Abubakar Kassim also said members held about 29,000 metric tonnes of finished NPK fertiliser that could be purchased and released immediately. He estimated the industry could make about 3.5 million bags available within the implementation period. The association said existing blending plants, warehouses and distribution networks were operating below capacity, despite demand for affordable farm inputs.

Budget and Economic Planning Minister Abubakar Bagudu said stakeholders had identified about 496,000 metric tonnes of fertiliser-related stocks as a starting point for the programme. A Ministry of Finance Incorporated representative separately reported about 90,000 metric tonnes of materials on the ground, with goods in transit bringing the combined amount to about 248,000 metric tonnes. The Bank of Agriculture and Bank of Industry have been approved as fund administrators and financial intermediaries. Shettima said restoring activity across the fertiliser value chain could support jobs and rural livelihoods, while the government said it would seek funding through other programmes to sustain the intervention.

title: Opposition Sets A Signing Date, But The Parties Still Want Different Things
summary: Nigeria’s opposition coalition plans to sign cooperation documents on 23 November. The summit has not resolved competing presidential ambitions or established a common ticket.
body:
Nigeria’s opposition coalition has set a date for its next step: a summit on 23 November at the NAF Conference Centre in Abuja. Participating parties are expected to sign a National Covenant for Democratic Renewal and a Framework for Opposition Unity, and adopt a National Reform Programme. The announcement gives a timetable for cooperation, but the documents have yet to be adopted and no common presidential arrangement has been confirmed.

The Coalition for Democracy, formerly G100, has proposed protecting votes at polling units as the parties’ first shared undertaking. That could provide a focus for cooperation even if the parties continue to back separate candidates. However, no public evidence has established joint funding, shared polling-agent deployment, functioning state committees or common operational procedures.

Recent reports name the ADC, APM, NDC, PDP, PRP and SDP as participants. Earlier coverage also listed the DLA, NRM and YPP, as well as specifying factional participation by the PDP. The shorter list does not establish that omitted parties have withdrawn. The summit will need to clarify who is represented and which participants have authority to make commitments.

The parties’ stated positions also indicate that cooperation has not settled the presidential contest. The NDC’s Osa Director said the party preferred that opposition figures unite around Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, while he could not confirm NDC involvement in reported Atiku Abubakar–Seyi Makinde negotiations. ADC representatives have confirmed opposition engagement but not a specific agreement with Makinde; reports of compromises have relied on unnamed sources. The APM has described that alliance as unfinished, while Makinde’s campaign says he is running to win and would serve one term.

Other participants have their own unresolved considerations. The PRP has expressed conditional willingness to respect a democratically agreed opposition choice, while rejecting the absorption of its party structures. The SDP is preparing its own campaign mobilisation, and a spokesman for the Turaki-led PDP faction says its candidates remain committed to cooperation. Neither position establishes a withdrawal or a binding commitment by the broader party. Attendance, authorised signatures, publication of the documents and evidence that instructions reach local organisations will help show whether the summit produces an electoral alliance or only continued engagement.

title: Jackson scores as Senegal move closer to 2027 AFCON
summary: Nicolas Jackson and El Hadji Malick Diouf scored in Senegal’s 4-2 win over Sudan. Senegal, Cameroon and Benin each have 10 points after four qualifying matches.
body:
Senegal moved closer to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after recovering from a second-half fightback to beat Sudan 4-2 on Monday. Nicolas Jackson opened the scoring in the fourth minute, and defender El Hadji Malick Diouf added a second midway through the first half. The match was played in South Sudan, where Sudan hosted the game because of civil war in its homeland.

Sudan fought back to level the score by the 75th minute, with substitute Al Gozoli Nooh and Salaheldin Adil finding the net. Senegal responded late: Pathe Mboup restored their lead before setting up Paul Mendy to score in added time. Jackson had also scored in Senegal’s 4-1 win over Sudan the previous Thursday. He arrived for the international matches after scoring nine goals in all competitions for Aston Villa this season.

Cameroon strengthened its position with a 3-0 victory over Namibia, while Benin secured a 1-0 win against the Central African Republic through debutant Ede Oloko’s added-time goal. Senegal, Cameroon and Benin each have 10 points from four matches and could be confirmed as qualifiers on Tuesday, depending on results elsewhere in their groups. The Central African Republic has now lost four consecutive matches.

In other games, Zimbabwe beat Equatorial Guinea 3-0, Guinea defeated Eritrea 3-1, and Ghana edged Somalia 1-0 through a Jordan Ayew penalty. Zimbabwe were the only host nation to play at home among Monday’s six matches; the Central African Republic, Eritrea and Namibia lack international-standard stadiums. Senegal is also awaiting a decision from the Court of Arbitration for Sport on its appeal against the Confederation of African Football’s ruling that Morocco were champions of the previous AFCON tournament.

title: [VIDEO] Bamayi: I’m Extremely Disappointed Security Agencies Allow That Joke To Go On — Sowunmi
summary: Segun Sowunmi criticised violence and poster destruction at a ‘Bamayi’ protest in Abuja, saying political opposition should be expressed at the ballot box.
body:
Segun Sowunmi has criticised a protest in Abuja where demonstrators chanted “Bamayi” at President Bola Tinubu’s motorcade. He said he was extremely disappointed with security agencies’ handling of the incident, which he described as incompatible with democratic conduct.

Sowunmi, a Peoples Democratic Party chieftain who is also a member of the All Progressives Congress campaign council, spoke on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He condemned the destruction of campaign posters and the reported use of violence by protesters.

He said people who oppose a candidate or campaign should express their views by voting rather than damaging property or carrying sticks. Sowunmi argued that such conduct was unacceptable and said he did not expect a responsible leader to engage in it.

The chants, which mean “we don’t want” in Hausa, were heard on November 13 after Tinubu attended Friday prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Abuja’s Garki area. Some protesters reportedly threw stones at the presidential convoy and destroyed APC campaign posters, prompting security operatives to intervene.

title: Uyo Book Club plans colloquium on Attah’s 88th birthday
summary: Uyo Book Club will hold a Friday colloquium for Victor Attah’s 88th birthday, examining his role in Akwa Ibom’s airport project. Aviation figures are expected.
body:
Uyo Book Club will hold a colloquium at 11 a.m. on Friday to mark former Akwa Ibom State governor Victor Attah’s 88th birthday. The event, at Watbridge Hotels and Suites in Uyo, will focus on the theme “Attah’s Vision in the Aviation Sector” and examine his contribution to the state’s aviation development. It will be free and open to the public.

The club’s founder, Udeme Nana, announced the event. Nana, a communication scholar and former head of the Department of Mass Communication at Akwa Ibom State Polytechnic, served as Attah’s spokesperson from 1999 to 2007. He said the gathering would consider the former governor’s vision for aviation infrastructure and its continuing effects.

Attah governed Akwa Ibom from 1999 to 2007. He conceived the state airport project and began construction before leaving office. Successive administrations completed the project and continued to develop the airport, which is named after him. It has since been expanded and includes a terminal building and a Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul facility.

Expected speakers include Mfon Udom, chairman of Ibom Air’s board; former Niger Delta Affairs Minister Umana Okon Umana; Ita Awak, a former director of airworthiness standards at the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority; and Augustine Okon, former chief executive of the defunct ADC Airline. They are expected to discuss the airport’s conception, development and significance, as well as the roles played by people involved in the project.

The colloquium is part of Uyo Book Club’s annual events recognising influential figures. The organisation also hosts reading sessions and literary discussions, and says its community has more than 7,000 members. It has previously held colloquia honouring Nigerian writers and journalists, including Ken Saro-Wiwa, John Pepper Clark, Wole Soyinka and Chinua Achebe.

title: Obi to publish Anambra achievements in 10-day series
summary: Peter Obi says he will publish a 10-day account of his Anambra governorship, responding to allegations that he neglected the state’s erosion crisis.
body:
Peter Obi, the Nigeria Democratic Congress’s 2027 presidential candidate, says he will publish a 10-day series detailing his record as governor of Anambra State. Titled “Record of Service,” it is set to begin on Tuesday and will describe his interventions, achievements and responsibilities during his tenure.

Obi announced the plan in a post on X on Monday, shortly after arriving in the United States for engagements in Washington, DC. He said he was making his record public in response to repeated scrutiny of his past and would present some of the accomplishments from his time as governor.

He addressed allegations that he abandoned Anambra during an erosion crisis, saying he had not avoided responsibilities entrusted to him. The accusations were also raised by President Bola Tinubu at an APC rally in Akwa Ibom on November 6, where Tinubu criticised Obi’s handling of erosion in the state and contrasted it with efforts to confront the Atlantic Ocean in Lagos.

Obi said his campaigns had focused on policies, ideas and practical solutions rather than personal criticism. He said he had given his best in each role he had held, while acknowledging that not every intended result could be achieved. He also said he would continue updating supporters on his engagements and other developments as campaign activity gathered momentum.

title: NNPC’s ₦210 trillion question: Not missing is not the same as accounted for, By Posi Olatubosun
summary: Former NNPC officials say ₦210 trillion in disputed balances was not lost but remains unexplained. A Senate committee is seeking detailed records from the company and its auditors.
body:
### NNPC’s ₦210 trillion balances raise questions over disclosure

Former Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) chief executive Mele Kyari has rejected claims that ₦210 trillion was lost during his tenure, describing the disputed figures as bookkeeping issues. His former chief financial officer and the former head of NAPIMS have made similar arguments before the Senate Public Accounts Committee. The figures are balance-sheet entries rather than cash reported to have been taken, but the committee is seeking explanations for how they were calculated and supported.

The committee’s review of NNPC audited financial statements from 2017 to 2023 identified about ₦103 trillion in accrued expenses and ₦107 trillion in sundry receivables. Lawmakers said the expenses included retention, legal and audit fees without specific breakdowns. NNPC attributed part of the balances to joint venture cash calls, but the committee questioned that account, noting that the cash call regime ended in January 2017. NNPC said the receivables were owed by defunct banks and other entities, but the debtors and individual amounts were not identified.

The accounting distinction is central to the dispute. Accrued expenses are liabilities for costs incurred but not yet paid; receivables are assets representing money owed to a company. Neither category alone demonstrates that cash has gone missing. However, the commentary argues that balances without identifiable counterparties or supporting evidence raise concerns about the reliability of the accounts. NNPC’s former chief financial officer told the committee that revenue over the seven-year period was about ₦54.5 trillion, a figure he cited to dispute that ₦210 trillion could have been lost. The commentary says that comparison also raises questions about the scale and composition of the reported balances.

The committee has asked NNPC’s auditors to provide a complete schedule of the receivables and payables, giving them one week in July, and rejected confidentiality as a reason to withhold it. The dispute has also included missed summonses and a warrant of arrest issued for Kyari in June after he failed to appear. The committee has raised separate questions about production costs and subsidy deductions. The commentary calls for NNPC to publish an itemised reconciliation, commission an independent forensic audit, and address any balances that cannot be substantiated. It also argues that the Financial Reporting Council should review the audits and that any necessary corrections to past accounts should be disclosed, particularly if NNPC proceeds with plans to list on the stock exchange.

title: NGX Group acquires 10% strategic stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
summary: NGX Group has acquired a 10% stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, extending its presence into East Africa. The move follows its investment in Ethiopia’s exchange.
body:
Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has acquired a 10% equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), extending its investment presence into East Africa. The Group said the move is part of its strategy to build regional leadership through partnerships and closer integration among African markets.

The investment gives NGX Group exposure to one of East Africa’s established capital markets and broadens its portfolio beyond Nigeria. It follows the Group’s strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, which it described as part of a long-term commitment to developing African capital market infrastructure.

NGX Group Chairman Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga characterised the Nairobi investment as a long-term commitment to market infrastructure and stronger financial links between West and East Africa. He said exchange groups could help shape cross-border capital flows by investing in the systems that support markets, while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.

Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Temi Popoola said the stake supports efforts to diversify the Group and strengthen its presence across African markets. He described Kenya as a key part of East Africa’s financial ecosystem and said the investment would broaden NGX Group’s potential sources of returns. Popoola also said a shareholding relationship could give lasting form to collaboration between the two markets, which he said had demonstrated benefits for issuers and investors.

The Group said it would continue to pursue investments intended to increase its regional participation, diversify returns and support more connected and competitive African capital markets. It also said its approach is guided by disciplined capital allocation and sustainable shareholder returns.

title: Lagos health providers demand fair tariffs, prompt payment of claims
summary: Lagos providers urged LASHMA to review tariffs, speed claims payments and include professional groups in ILERA EKO. The agency said it would address the concerns.
body:
Healthcare providers in Lagos State have urged the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA) to review reimbursement rates, pay claims promptly and ensure health professionals are included in the implementation of the ILERA EKO insurance programme. The requests were made during a visit by the newly elected executives of the Healthcare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos State Branch, to LASHMA Permanent Secretary Dr Emmanuella Zamba on November 11, 2026.

HCPAN Lagos chairman Adekoya Abimbola Julius said fair and sustainable operating conditions for facilities were essential to expanding coverage and achieving Universal Health Coverage. He cited low reimbursement rates, delays in processing and paying claims, complicated enrolment procedures and limited professional involvement as issues requiring attention. He also called for simpler enrolment, stronger engagement with providers and recognition of the professional groups affiliated with HCPAN.

Zamba acknowledged the concerns and said LASHMA would give them attention. She said reimbursement rates were due for review after the stipulated two-year period and expressed hope that an adjustment could be made in 2027. She also noted that rates were influenced by the premiums affordable to enrollees, and said the agency would work to improve claims processing and payment mechanisms.

The agency briefed the delegation on its operations and the state’s health insurance policy, including provider onboarding into ILERA EKO, Provider-Led Enrolment, LASHMA-AID and its quality assurance framework. Former HCPAN Nigeria president Dr Jimmy Adeyeye Arigbabuwo called for continued training to help providers and other stakeholders understand their roles and reduce operational challenges. Former HCPAN Lagos chairman Pharmacist Biola Paul-Ozieh urged the parties to maintain dialogue and cooperation. Zamba also expressed willingness to take part in HCPAN’s proposed retreat and webinar series.

title: Tanzania vs Nigeria: Super Eagles arrive in Zanzibar for crucial clash
summary: Nigeria’s Super Eagles have arrived in Zanzibar for Tuesday’s AFCON qualifier after beating Tanzania 3-1 in the first leg. Ademola Lookman is out with a knee sprain.
body:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles have arrived in Zanzibar for Tuesday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying match against Tanzania. The delegation travelled on Sunday, two days after a 3-1 home win in the first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. It included 23 players, coaches, support staff, officials and selected journalists, as well as supporters’ club members.

Nigeria took an early lead through Alhassan Yusuf in the second minute, but Tanzania equalised through Alphonce Msanga in the 32nd. Substitute Tolu Arokodare scored twice after coming on at half-time, finding the net in the 52nd minute and again eight minutes later. The teams will meet at Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar for the return fixture.

The result lifted Nigeria’s hopes in Group L, where the team have six points from three matches and sit second, one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau. Nigeria opened their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar before losing 3-0 away to Guinea-Bissau. Tanzania are already assured of a place at the tournament as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda, leaving the group’s remaining qualification place contested by Nigeria and Guinea-Bissau.

Nigeria will be without forward Ademola Lookman, who sustained a knee ligament sprain during Friday’s match and has been ruled out of the return fixture. He contributed to the opening goal in Uyo before being substituted in the first half. A positive result in Zanzibar would support Nigeria’s bid to secure qualification, with Guinea-Bissau also competing for the group’s remaining place.

title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
summary: England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid to end the world champions’ 44-game competitive unbeaten run. The win secured England top spot in Nations League group A3.
body:
England defeated Spain 3-2 in Madrid on Sunday, ending the world champions’ 44-game unbeaten run in competitive matches and securing top spot in Nations League group A3. Both teams had already qualified to progress, but England’s group-winning position means the side will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March.

Harry Kane opened the scoring with a penalty just before half-time after Spain defender Pau Cubarsi brought him down in the area. England extended their lead soon after the break: Ezri Konsa headed in from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute, then Ben White finished a move involving Kane and Jude Bellingham four minutes later.

Spain responded after Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the area. Mikel Oyarzabal converted the resulting penalty, and Nico Williams reduced the deficit further after receiving a pass from Yamal. His shot struck the post before going in.

Spain pressed for an equaliser, but England held on. Goalkeeper James Trafford made saves from Yamal and Marc Cucurella as the hosts tried to complete their comeback. The defeat was Spain’s first in a competitive match since March 2023, when their current unbeaten sequence began.

title: Tinubu’s five-year defence plan ready to tackle insecurity – APC Campaign Council
summary: APC’s campaign council says Tinubu’s five-year defence plan is ready to guide security investment. It also cites approved expansions to military and police numbers.
body:
The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council says President Bola Tinubu’s proposed Five-Year Strategic Defence Operations Plan is ready. In a statement issued Sunday, spokesperson Dele Alake described it as a framework for coordinating defence priorities, operational needs, capability development and spending in response to current and anticipated security threats.

The council said the plan is intended to support a more coordinated, intelligence-led and technology-enabled approach to security, combining prevention with military operations. It reported that operations over the administration’s last three years had eliminated more than 15,000 terrorists and bandits. It also said more than 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependants had surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, the government’s rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents. The council presented the figures as evidence of a strategy combining military action with non-military measures.

The statement said Tinubu had approved four new Army divisions and changes to existing formations to broaden operational coverage. It also cited approval for two Army depots, in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State. Each facility can train 6,000 recruits at a time, according to the council; 5,210 recruits are currently training in Osogbo. The council said the depots are expected to speed up recruitment and increase the number of soldiers available for deployment. It added that the President had approved 28,000 additional soldiers and 50,000 additional police officers.

The council also pointed to investment in military accommodation and operational facilities, including a 700-unit barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State. It said the plan would guide security-sector investment according to identified threats and national priorities, strengthen readiness and address capability gaps while making better use of available resources. The proposed framework forms part of what the council described as broader investment in personnel, equipment, technology, training and infrastructure.

title: Troops Repel Terrorists’ Attacks In Zamfara, Recover Weapons In Kaduna
summary: Troops repelled attacks on two communities in Zamfara and conducted operations in Kaduna, where one suspected terrorist was killed and weapons and other items recovered.
body:
Troops from the Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, repelled successive attacks on communities in Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State on November 14, 2026. The Theatre Command said armed men on motorcycles attacked Wuya and Yarzabia, but troops from Sector Two forced them to retreat with superior firepower. The attackers regrouped and launched another assault, which troops also repelled while holding their positions.

Reinforcements later extended operations to neighbouring communities, and patrols continued to deter further incursions. The operation’s Air Component deployed a combat aircraft to support ground forces. The Theatre Command said the aircraft spotted terrorists moving a large herd of suspected rustled cattle away from the affected communities and carried out multiple airstrikes, reportedly neutralising scores of attackers.

In Kaduna State, Sector One troops conducted a fighting patrol near farmlands in Aguba Village, Kajuru Local Government Area, following intelligence about suspected terrorist activity. They exchanged fire with suspects, killing one, while others fled. A search of the area turned up two fabricated rifles, a mobile phone, substances suspected to be cannabis and other illicit drugs, and recharge cards.

In a separate incident, troops deployed along Buruku-Kaduna Road engaged armed suspects after receiving reports of their movement. The suspects fled into a nearby forest, leaving behind two motorcycles, which troops recovered. Pursuit and search operations were continuing to prevent them from regrouping. The Theatre Command praised the troops and urged the public to provide security agencies with timely, credible information.

title: 2027 Poll: Zamfara APC constitutes 900-member gubernatorial campaign council
summary: Zamfara APC has formed a campaign council of more than 900 members for the 2027 general elections. Governor Dauda Lawal will chair the body.
body:
The Zamfara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress has constituted a campaign council of more than 900 members to coordinate the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Secretary to the State Government Abubakar Mohammad Nakwada announced the formation in a statement on Sunday. He will also serve as the council’s secretary-general.

The council was formed after consultations and recommendations by the state party chapter, and was approved by Governor Dauda Lawal and the party’s state leadership. Lawal will chair the body, with Deputy Governor Mani Mummuni and state APC chairman Kabiru Moyi B. Magaji serving as vice-chairmen.

Elder statesman Salihu Maibuhu Gummi was named director-general, while Dr Sani Ahmad Sambo will be the council’s spokesperson. The body is tasked with coordinating and driving the APC’s campaign activities in Zamfara as the party seeks victory in the forthcoming election.

The council is expected to focus on issue-based campaigning and presenting the administration’s achievements over the past three years. Its members were urged to show commitment, unity, discipline and dedication, and to comply with the Electoral Act and guidelines issued by the Independent National Electoral Commission.

title: Presidency lists eight projects in North Central under Tinubu
summary: The Presidency has outlined eight areas of North Central development under Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, including transport, power, agriculture and security. The projects also cover education, skills and regional development.
body:
The Presidency has listed projects and programmes across eight areas of development in Nigeria’s North Central region under President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Sunday Dare, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Public Communication and spokesperson, shared the list in a post on X on Sunday. The areas are transport, aviation, power, agriculture, women and youth empowerment, education, security and regional development.

Road projects include a dual carriageway along the Mararaban Jama’a–Pankshin–Langtang–Shendam–River Ibi corridor, Phase II rehabilitation of the Babban-Lamba–Sharan Road and construction of the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Biu–Maiduguri Superhighway. The list also includes a 600-metre Akwanga underpass, the Lafia Bypass, reconstruction of the Bali–Serti–Gembu Road and improvements to the Jalingo–Wukari corridor. Construction of the Gembu–Mbamnga–Yang Road began in early 2025. In aviation, the Presidency cited approval for an airstrip on the Mambilla Plateau.

Energy projects include a 40-megawatt hydropower plant at Kashimbila Multipurpose Dam, expected to supply the national grid, and irrigation channels intended to support year-round farming. The list also includes solar mini-grids, streetlights and home systems. Agricultural measures include distributing improved seedlings and fertiliser, training farmers, supporting hybrid potato farming, expanding irrigated land and developing processing centres.

For women and young people, the listed interventions include agricultural support through the First Lady’s Renewed Hope Initiative, vocational training and certification, start-up grants, business training and tools for market women, and rural grants and skills programmes. Education measures include transforming Federal Polytechnic, Nasarawa, into the Federal University of Mining, Engineering and Technology, as well as expanding scholarship and higher-education opportunities.

The security plans include establishing a new Army division in Jalingo, Taraba State, and increasing deployments to protect farming communities. The eighth area is regional development, including the North Central Development Commission and federal road projects intended to improve connectivity. The Federal Government says the broader agenda is aimed at improving infrastructure, supporting economic activity and expanding development opportunities.

title: DMO offers N2 trillion FGN bonds on Monday as N3.37 trillion inflows hit the system
summary: The DMO plans a N2 trillion FGN bond auction on Nov. 16. It comes amid N3.37 trillion in expected inflows and a N3.97 trillion liquidity surplus.
body: Recent auction activity suggests the DMO may restrict allotments rather than accept substantially higher borrowing costs. The stop rate on the 364-day Treasury Bill fell to 15.80% from 15.90%. Investors will be watching the accepted yields across the four bond maturities, while the final allotment and stop rates will indicate how the DMO balances funding needs with borrowing costs.

title: Odumodublvck set to make acting debut in TG Omori’s ‘The Rise of the Machine’
summary: Odumodublvck will make his acting debut in TG Omori’s short film The Rise of the Machine. The film was screened at AFRIFF’s 2026 closing gala.
body:
Rapper Odumodublvck is making his acting debut in The Rise of the Machine, a short film directed by cinematographer TG Omori. The pair attended the closing ceremony and awards gala of the Africa International Film Festival on November 7, 2026, where the film was screened. Odumodublvck is also a co-producer and executive producer on the project, while it marks Omori’s debut as a film director.

In a recent interview, Odumodublvck said he had been interested in acting since his school years, when he took part in drama clubs. He described film as a way to show aspects of his creative work that music alone might not convey. The short film, he said, is an extension of his recent projects, The Machine Is Coming and The Industry Machine.

The film is also a precursor to a forthcoming project of the same name, which is intended to complete the rapper’s Machine Trilogy. The first instalment, The Machine Is Coming, featured the songs Legolas and Pity This Boy, with Victony. It was nominated for Best Rap Album and Album of the Year at the 18th Headies.

The follow-up, The Industry Machine, included the title track and If You Like Gym. The latter received a nomination for Best Rap Single at the 16th Headies. The Rise of the Machine was filmed in Lagos State and is scheduled for release later in 2026, ahead of the new project. The film adds acting and filmmaking roles to Odumodublvck’s work as a recording artist.

title: 2027: Udeh unveils ATM support group for Tinubu, Mbah, APC candidates
summary: Kingsley Udeh launched the ATM group to mobilise support for APC candidates in 2027. It plans to use digital tools to track membership and voter outreach.
body:
Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology Kingsley Udeh has inaugurated As Tinubu and Mbah Move (ATM), a support group campaigning for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah and other APC candidates in the 2027 elections. The group says it will use technology to organise voter outreach and monitor activity across Enugu State’s 4,145 polling units.

At the launch, Mbah urged members to take the enthusiasm from the event into communities, families and polling units. He said the group’s success would depend on whether it converted that energy into grassroots engagement and electoral support. He encouraged members to point voters to projects including Smart Green Schools, the International Conference Centre, the Presidential Hotel and the International Hospital. He also acknowledged that poverty, unreliable electricity, water shortages and unpaved roads remained challenges in some communities.

Mbah made the case for Tinubu’s re-election, describing the President as a unifier and defending the removal of the fuel subsidy and the unification of foreign exchange rates as difficult reforms intended to support economic stability and investment. He also cited federal infrastructure projects in the South-East, including work on the Enugu-Onitsha and Enugu-Port Harcourt highways, and the concessioning of Akanu Ibiam International Airport. He said cargo operations and direct flights between Enugu and Guangzhou, China, were planned before the end of the first quarter of 2027. Mbah urged South-East voters to build alliances beyond the region and warned APC members against complacency.

Udeh said ATM would use an innovation situation room and digital dashboard to track membership, recruitment and mobilisation. Registration will require a Permanent Voter Card and voters’ identification details submitted through an online portal, he said. The governor will have access to the dashboard to review membership figures and activity. Udeh described the initiative as a data-driven alternative to unverified membership claims and pledged measurable support for APC candidates.

Mbah urged eligible voters to collect their voter cards ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections and the February 6 governorship and State Assembly polls. The event included the swearing-in of group members and executives at state and local government levels. APC officials and other political and community representatives also attended.

title: Why I abandoned law for acting – Femi Adebayo
summary: Femi Adebayo left litigation in 2005, saying acting offered greater financial rewards and fulfilment. His father had hoped he would pursue law.
body:
Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo says he left legal practice in 2005 to pursue acting and film production, drawn by the work’s financial rewards and the greater fulfilment it brought him. He discussed the decision in an interview on the Afrobeats podcast, published on Saturday, reflecting on his career and his upbringing in an entertainment family.

Adebayo was called to the Nigerian Bar in 2003 and spent about two years practising litigation. He said he appeared in court and handled cases before deciding to leave law. Acting, which began as a hobby, had become the work he felt more passionate about, he explained, and he found it made him happier than the career he had studied for.

He said his father, veteran actor Adebayo Salami, known as Oga Bello, initially welcomed his choice to study law. Salami had wanted to become a lawyer himself but, according to his son, lacked the financial resources to pursue legal studies. Adebayo said his father’s reaction to his eventual departure from law was mixed: he was glad his son was following him into acting, but had also hoped to see him continue in the profession he had once wanted for himself.

Adebayo said his father later became grateful for the path he chose. His work has since extended across several parts of filmmaking, including acting, producing, writing and directing. His account describes a transition from a short period in litigation to a full-time career in entertainment, shaped by both personal interest and the practical rewards he saw in the industry.

title: Police Arrest Two Suspects For Staging Abduction In Ebonyi
summary: Police in Ebonyi arrested two people accused of staging a kidnapping to seek ₦30 million. The alleged victim’s father reported the abduction on October 31.
body:
Police in Ebonyi State have arrested two suspects over an alleged plot to stage a kidnapping and demand money. The case began at about 10:30 p.m. on October 31, 2026, when the father of one of the suspects contacted the police control room to report that his son had been abducted from his hostel in Ikwo Local Government Area.

Police spokesperson SP Joshua Ukandu said the father had received view-once videos and voice notes showing his son bound and apparently held captive. The people claiming to be the abductors demanded ₦30 million and threatened to kill the young man if the money was not paid.

Ukandu said police launched an intelligence-led investigation into the reported abduction. After sustained surveillance and discreet inquiries, officers arrested the two suspects on the night of November 5, 2026, as they came out of the room where they had been hiding, he said. The statement did not provide further details about the suspects or indicate whether charges had been filed.

Ebonyi State Commissioner of Police CP Hope Urunwa Okafor warned against staging kidnappings or making false abduction claims. She said such schemes cause serious distress to families and divert police resources from genuine security threats, adding that the conduct is a criminal offence punishable under the law.

title: US Air Force captain arrested in Japan
summary: Japanese police arrested a 27-year-old US Air Force captain on suspicion of drunk driving in Okinawa. Whether he breached a US military curfew is unclear.
body:
Japanese police arrested a 27-year-old US Air Force captain on suspicion of drunk driving in Okinawa on Saturday. A prefectural police spokesman said the man was driving in Okinawa City at about 3:09 a.m. The captain was assigned to Kadena Air Base, according to a report by Kyodo News.

Police said it was unclear whether the captain had violated a curfew imposed by US officials. The base did not immediately provide comment.

The arrest came a week after Japan and the United States agreed on measures to prevent crimes by US service members in Okinawa. The agreement followed public anger over a murder allegedly involving an American Marine.

About 54,000 US military personnel are stationed in Japan, most of them in Okinawa. US officials had also announced an extension of a curfew for lower-ranking service members through December 7 and a ban on all service members drinking alcohol outside their homes between midnight and 5 a.m.

title: Tinubu flags off construction of $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport
summary: Nigeria has launched the $3.5bn Bakassi Deep Seaport project after years of delay. Plans include a 20-metre-draft port and a 260-kilometre cargo highway.
body: Otu said the port would encourage investment in logistics, trade, fishing, shipping, tourism and shipbuilding. His administration is training selected residents for work during construction and operations, while acknowledging that foreign technical expertise may also be needed. Nigerian Ports Authority Managing Director Abubakar Dantsoho said the port could strengthen trade links with landlocked countries including Chad, Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso. Afreximbank said the investment could expand port capacity and support trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area. Tinubu also said Nigeria’s blue economy could generate $44 billion annually if the country captured cargo traffic now moving through neighbouring countries.

title: 2027: Aaro Meta urges Kwara South APC to back Danladi
summary: Aaro Meta urged Kwara South APC members to back Yakubu Salihu Danladi for 2027, citing fairness among the state’s three senatorial districts. It also called for party unity.
body:
Political group Aaro Meta has urged aggrieved All Progressives Congress members in Kwara South to reconcile and support the party’s governorship candidate, Kwara State House of Assembly Speaker Yakubu Salihu Danladi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The group also endorsed a candidate from Kwara North, saying political power should be shared fairly among the state’s three senatorial districts.

Coordinator Adebayo S. Daramola made the appeal on Friday at a News Keg event organised by the Nigeria Union of Journalists’ Correspondents’ Chapel in Ilorin. He said Aaro Meta had supported the 2018 O to Ge movement, which contributed to the APC-led government taking office in 2019, and argued that sustaining the party’s electoral prospects required unity and fairness.

The group recalled that it backed an APC candidate from Kwara Central in the 2019 governorship election despite being based in Kwara South. That candidate, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, won the election and secured a second term in 2023. Aaro Meta said Kwara South should show similar political accommodation by supporting Danladi, rather than allowing divisions over preferred aspirants to weaken the party.

Aaro Meta said Kwara South had produced a governor for eight years since 1999, while Kwara Central would have accounted for 20 years in office by the end of AbdulRazaq’s tenure in May 2027. It appealed particularly to dissatisfied APC members and the G-15 political bloc to work for Danladi and other party candidates, warning that internal disputes could give opposition parties an advantage.

The group also praised President Bola Tinubu and Governor AbdulRazaq for efforts to address banditry and kidnapping, saying insecurity in Kwara South had declined. It identified the Oro Forest corridor, from Oro-Ago and Oreke Road towards Egbe, Okoloke and Lade, as a continuing concern. It described military bases in Oro-Ago and Babanla, and the 184 Battalion in Omu-Aran, as strategic to tackling the threat.

title: Who Gets To Compete?
summary: Campaigns are advancing and opposition talks continue. Violence, legal uncertainty and INEC’s preparations are testing access and confidence in the 2027 vote.
body:
Who Gets To Compete?

As campaigns gather pace and opposition figures discuss cooperation, questions about access, legal certainty and confidence in the vote are becoming central to the contest. Recent events have ranged from Peter Obi’s visit to a community affected by violence to an APC mobilisation rally and public questions about the electoral commission’s preparations. Together, they highlight that competing for votes also depends on candidates being able to organise and citizens being able to participate safely.

A reported attack on an NDC town hall gathering in Oregun, Lagos, left participants injured, according to reporting from the scene, and a suspect was arrested. The NDC alleged political responsibility, while the Lagos APC denied sponsoring the incident. The available reporting did not establish independent evidence linking the attackers to a political party. An investigation must determine who was responsible; meanwhile, political meetings should be accessible without fear of assault. Intimidation can deter attendees, volunteers and venues, affecting the conditions in which candidates compete.

Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde confirmed active discussions involving Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, saying any decision should consider evidence, manifestos, past performance and public sentiment. He did not announce an agreement or endorse a candidate. Separately, INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission would comply with binding court decisions concerning Atiku’s participation and noted that it faces more than 300 pending cases. The ADC says it has appealed a November 5 ruling and sought a stay of execution; the material available does not establish that a stay has been granted. The dispute remains unresolved in the information provided.

Obi visited people affected by the June 2025 attack in Yelwata, announced support for orphaned children’s education and a borehole, and held a town hall in Makurdi with running mate Rabiu Kwankwaso. In Akure, Vice-President Kashim Shettima represented President Bola Tinubu at an APC rally, calling for unity and mobilisation. The campaign set a target of 1.2 million votes in Ondo, an aspiration rather than a forecast. Rally activity and organisation do not establish how voters will decide.

INEC has announced a nationwide mock accreditation exercise for November 28 to test accreditation and electronic result transmission. Amupitan said the commission had procured additional BVAS devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned to each machine from 1,250 to 850. The exercise’s effectiveness remains to be tested; transparent findings on performance, problems and corrective steps would help voters assess the commission’s assurances. No fresh, credible polling in the material reviewed establishes a national shift. The standard for the coming weeks is whether lawful contenders can be heard, citizens can participate without intimidation and votes can be counted credibly.

title: Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade
summary: President Bola Tinubu said the Bakassi Deep Seaport will widen Nigeria’s trade routes and create jobs. The project is designed to ease pressure on Lagos ports.
body:
Tinubu Hails Bakassi Seaport, Says Project Will Create Jobs, Boost Trade

President Bola Tinubu has described the groundbreaking of the Bakassi Deep Seaport in Cross River State as a step towards diversifying Nigeria’s economy, expanding trade and creating jobs. Vice President Kashim Shettima represented him at the ceremony in Bakassi on Friday, November 13, 2026. Tinubu commended Governor Bassey Otu and the state’s residents for advancing a project first conceived in 2014.

Designed with a 20-metre draft, the port is intended to receive large vessels that currently bypass Nigerian ports. A planned 260-kilometre superhighway would connect it to markets across the country. Tinubu said the facility would complement Lagos, which handles more than 80 per cent of Nigeria’s foreign trade, by easing congestion and reducing the country’s reliance on a single maritime gateway. He said Nigeria handles only a fraction of regional cargo trade despite the importance of sea transport to commerce.

Tinubu credited Otu with helping to address institutional and financial obstacles, including efforts to secure a $3.5 billion financing arrangement with Afreximbank and formalise the project’s Public-Private Partnership framework in February 2025. Otu said the groundbreaking followed years of political, administrative, legal and environmental challenges. He cited an initial funding approval of $2.27 billion, federal approval for the project and preparatory work including environmental, hydrographic, geotechnical and geophysical studies.

Otu said the port could support employment and business in logistics, shipping, fishing, tourism and shipbuilding. Selected Cross River residents are receiving specialised training for construction and operational roles, he said. The governor also pointed to a corridor linking the state’s airport, seaport and Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as a route for cargo and investment, and invited maritime-sector investors to consider opportunities in the state.

Marine and Blue Economy Minister Gboyega Oyetola pledged his ministry’s support for a modern, efficient and environmentally sustainable port. He said the project could improve market access and create industrial and employment opportunities, with benefits extending beyond Cross River. Tinubu urged residents to protect the project from political interference and described it as an investment for future generations.

title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
summary: Lagos APM candidate Prince Laja Adeoye condemned an attack that disrupted an NDC town hall in Ikeja. He called for arrests and protection of political gatherings.
body:
Lagos State governorship candidate Prince Laja Adeoye of the Action Peoples Movement has condemned an attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress supporters at a town hall meeting in Ikeja, calling the disruption a threat to democracy. The meeting was held on Thursday at Classique Event Centre in Oregun.

Adeoye said disrupting the gathering infringed on citizens’ rights to assemble and express political views. He warned that attacks on opposition events could increase political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also said the incident was especially concerning in Lagos, which he described as a traditional centre of political activity.

The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible, regardless of their political affiliation or status. He cautioned that failing to hold perpetrators accountable could encourage similar incidents elsewhere. Adeoye also raised concerns about the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, citing reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and had working equipment taken.

Adeoye commended NDC supporters for not retaliating and called on political leaders and parties to discourage violence and focus campaigns on issues. He urged INEC, security agencies and other stakeholders to work together to ensure fair conditions for all parties, and called on the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to promote peaceful political engagement. He also sympathised with people reportedly injured in the attack and urged the NDC to continue its campaign. Adeoye said the APM remained committed to peaceful, credible and transparent elections and respect for the rule of law.

title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences – Report
summary: Malaysian authorities arrested 112 African nationals in immigration operations from January through October 31, including 53 Nigerians. Most were detained for lacking valid permits.
body:
Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians in immigration operations

Malaysia’s Immigration Department arrested 112 African nationals in enforcement operations conducted across the country between January and October 31, according to figures disclosed by department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. Nigerians made up the largest group, with 53 arrests, followed by 13 Ugandans, 10 Kenyans and eight Ghanaians.

The remaining arrests included six each from Somalia and Tanzania, four from Senegal, three from Algeria, and two each from Burkina Faso, Togo and The Gambia. One person each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also detained.

Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or staying in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. That offence accounted for 85 arrests, including 47 Nigerians. A further 23 people were detained for overstaying under Section 15(1)(c), while three were arrested for breaching the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested over alleged possession of forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Act.

Authorities separately arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid passes. Shaaban said enforcement operations were intended to address undocumented migration and take action against employers who employ or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. The report did not identify the Nigerians arrested or specify where they were apprehended.

title: Best performing money market funds in Nigeria as of October 2026
summary: First Ally led Nigeria’s money market funds in October with a 21.17% year-to-date yield. Sector assets rose 5.05% to N6.90 trillion.
body:
First Ally Money Market Fund retained the top position in Nigeria’s money market fund rankings in October 2026, recording a year-to-date yield of 21.17%. The sector’s net asset value reached N6.90 trillion as of October 30, up 5.05% from N6.56 trillion in September. It comprised 50 funds following the addition of Custodian Money Market Fund and represented 68.31% of the N10.09 trillion mutual fund market.

DLM Money Market Fund placed second with a 20.47% yield, followed by Coronation at 20.31%, RT Briscoe Savings & Investment Fund at 20.19%, Page at 19.53% and Custodian at 19.52%. CardinalStone recorded 19.38%, Zedcrest 19.12%, Apel Wealth 18.98% and STL 18.93% to complete the top 10. STL narrowly held the final place, finishing 0.01 percentage point ahead of the fund ranked 11th, Comercio Partners.

Yields at the top of the table generally eased during the month: six of the seven funds that remained in the top 10 recorded lower year-to-date yields than in September. The top-10 entry threshold also declined, from 19.01% to 18.93%. CardinalStone was the exception, rising 0.07 percentage point to 19.38%. Custodian and Zedcrest entered the top 10, while Page returned after last appearing in August. First Ally’s yield fell from 21.43% in September, but it remained ahead of DLM by 0.70 percentage point.

Money market funds continue to attract retail and institutional investors seeking liquid options focused on capital preservation. Their returns remained attractive even as fixed-income yields moderated following the Central Bank of Nigeria’s September reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate from 26.5% to 23%. On the reported year-to-date figures, a hypothetical N5 million investment in First Ally at the start of the year would have generated about N1,058,500 in returns by October. Coronation was the largest fund in the top 10, with N126.28 billion in assets, while RT Briscoe was the smallest, with N736.06 million.

title: Atiku wanted me as running mate in 2023 – Makinde
summary: Seyi Makinde says Atiku Abubakar asked him to be running mate in 2023, but he declined, citing limited experience. He also discussed the PDP, governance and security.
body:
Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde says former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar approached him to be his running mate in the 2023 presidential election. Makinde said he declined because he had spent only three years as governor and felt he lacked enough experience in public service to take on the role. He discussed the offer and other aspects of his political career in an interview.

Makinde also spoke about the G5 governors’ opposition to Atiku’s 2023 bid and the continuing crisis in the Peoples Democratic Party. He said he was the only member of the G5 who had since left the party. He defended his faction’s decision to expel former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike, saying it was intended to enable the PDP to contest the election, even with a weakened structure. Makinde also questioned the state of democracy, citing disputes over the nullification of candidates less than 80 days before a national election.

Responding to claims by the Oyo State All Progressives Congress that he had neglected governance for political activity, Makinde said state administration was continuing. He pointed to his presentation of the 2027 budget estimates to the State House of Assembly and his state-of-the-state address. He also said his preferred successor, former commissioner Bimbo Adekanbi, should develop his own political identity, and rejected the description of himself as a political godfather.

On security, Makinde backed decentralised decision-making and state police, arguing that states should be able to tailor responses to local conditions. He said safeguards would be needed to address concerns that state policing could be used oppressively. Referring to kidnappings of pupils and teachers in Oyo and Borno states, he said Oyo had secured the release of those abducted, though the incident involved casualties. Makinde said a judicial panel had submitted its report on the Oyo incident and that a government white paper was due within the week.

title: Beside Adamawa Government House, school battles decay, thirst
summary: Dougirei Secondary School in Yola lacks reliable water, safe classrooms and basic learning facilities. Parents and staff are urging Adamawa officials to address the problems.
body:
Beside Adamawa Government House, school battles decay and thirst

Dougirei Secondary School, in Yola North Local Government Area, is less than 100 metres behind the Adamawa State Government House. Yet pupils and staff face deteriorating classrooms, insufficient desks and chairs, no functional water supply and a shortage of other basic facilities. During a visit, teachers and some students were seen working under trees, while the staff room shared by the junior and senior sections was described as too cramped for personnel.

Classroom ceilings are falling apart, raising concerns about safety. The school has no working water supply, leaving its toilets closed and students to use nearby bushes. It also lacks an examination hall: students sitting external examinations, including WAEC and NECO, have had to do so outdoors, using stones as seats. Staff said science subjects are taught without a laboratory, limiting opportunities for practical lessons. Some teachers bring mats to use as seats and work surfaces.

Flooding adds to the difficulties during the rainy season. Water discharged through drainage pipes from Government House is reportedly channelled into the school grounds, sometimes disrupting lessons and prompting the management to suspend activities over safety concerns. Parents-Teachers Association chairman Alhaji Mohammed Usman said he had written several times to the Ministry of Education without receiving a satisfactory response.

The school’s condition has prompted questions about how the state’s education priorities are being implemented. The administration has introduced free education and school feeding in boarding schools and has announced plans for model secondary schools across the state’s 21 local government areas. Budget figures cited in the report show education allocations of N17.32bn in 2020, N24bn in 2021, N17.3bn in 2022, N26.8bn in 2023, N15.603bn in 2024, N40.41bn in 2025 and N40.63bn in 2026. Stakeholders are calling for greater transparency over how the funding is used and for action on basic school infrastructure. The education commissioner was unavailable for comment, and calls had not been returned by the time the report was filed.

title: Lagos taskforce raids Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja, arrests 3 suspected drug peddlers
summary: Lagos State Taskforce raids in Cele, Itire and Ilasamaja led to three arrests over alleged drug sales. The suspects pleaded not guilty in court.
body:
The Lagos State Taskforce says it has arrested three people in raids on suspected criminal hideouts in Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja and other parts of the state. The operation was led by the agency’s chairman, Chief Superintendent of Police Adetayo Akerele, and targeted locations identified as hotspots for drug activity and public disturbances.

The agency alleges the suspects sold and distributed marijuana, Colorado and Indian hemp to adults, underage people and street urchins around Cele Bus Stop, Itire and Ilasamaja. It said the activity had reportedly contributed to public disturbances, street fights, cult-related activity and youth violence in the affected communities.

The suspects were identified as Bello Musa, 18, and Abubakar Musa, 27, both of Adebayo Street, Cele-Ijesha, and Agboola Fuad, 24, of Sewage Street, Abaranje, Ijegun. According to the taskforce, they have been arraigned on three counts relating to possession and sale of illicit drugs, inciting members of the public against officers carrying out lawful duties, and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace. All three pleaded not guilty. The case was adjourned until December 9, 2026, for further proceedings.

During the operation in Itire, Akerele thanked a whistleblower and residents for their cooperation. He said public participation and timely sharing of information helped identify and remove suspected criminal elements from communities. Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Bolade, Oshodi, he urged residents to report suspicious activity and work with law enforcement.

Akerele also warned young people against drug activity, street violence and cultism, and urged them to avoid associations that could expose them to criminality. He said the taskforce would continue enforcement against drug peddling, environmental nuisances and other criminal activity, and warned that those who violate applicable laws would face legal consequences.

title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
summary: Lawmakers are seeking answers about the Trump administration’s knowledge of Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China. The inquiry also covers chip exports.
body:
US lawmakers from both parties are calling for answers about what the Trump administration knew of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected by US intelligence of working for China. The scrutiny intensified Thursday after Nvidia’s board announced Huang’s immediate departure as chief executive. China has denied the allegations against the woman, Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed; the two are not related. Jensen Huang acknowledged the affair on Sunday.

The controversy has renewed debate over US sales of advanced chips to China. Jensen Huang had advocated looser export rules, while lawmakers are also questioning Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to restrict sales. Reports have said President Donald Trump was informed of the suspicions last year and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said Monday that the FBI was looking into the affair and that Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy.

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Congress should seek answers from Huang and Nvidia about possible risks to national security. He also questioned what the administration did after learning of the relationship, including whether officials were told not to investigate, and what Trump knew when he invited Huang aboard Air Force One for a state visit to China in May. Senate Republican leader John Thune said a congressional investigation would make sense given the national security stakes.

Three Republican House committee chairmen have said they want to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democratic lawmakers are also preparing to examine the matter: the top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees wrote to Lutnick Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s approval and taxation of chip exports to Chinese firms linked to China’s government and military. They accused Lutnick and Trump of overlooking a national security threat despite reportedly being informed of the suspicions.

Democrats may also examine potential conflicts of interest. Nvidia has said its reported $25 million pledge toward a White House ballroom project was unrelated to its business interests; the pledge reportedly came months after chip sales to China resumed. The calls for scrutiny come days before Trump is due to travel to China.

title: FG hands Port Harcourt airport to private operator for 30 years
summary: Nigeria has granted Port Harcourt Airport Company a 30-year concession for the Port Harcourt airport. The government says the deal aims to improve operations and attract investment.
body:
The Federal Government has granted Port Harcourt Airport Company Ltd. a 30-year concession to operate the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. Aviation and Aerospace Development Minister Festus Keyamo announced the agreement at a signing ceremony in Abuja on Thursday. He said the arrangement had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council.

Keyamo said the concession was intended to ease the cost of running airports that operate at a loss and attract private investment. The government currently uses profits from major airports to support less profitable facilities, he said. Airport expenses include staff, electricity and diesel for generators, while the government has limited resources to develop commercial services beyond passenger and aircraft operations. Private participation, he added, could improve efficiency and help airports generate more revenue.

The minister said earlier administrations had tried to concession the Port Harcourt airport but faced resistance from aviation unions and lengthy legal disputes. The current administration engaged with unions to address workers’ concerns and safeguard their welfare, he said. Speaking for the concessionaire, R28 Holdings Group Executive Eyo Asuquo said the deal would create jobs rather than lead to job losses. He also pledged substantial infrastructure investment, with the aim of bringing the airport up to standards comparable to facilities in Europe and the United States.

The government has also received concession proposals for Benin Airport and Yola International Airport. The Port Harcourt agreement follows the formal concession of Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, signed on January 21, 2026. The deals are part of the government’s effort to bring private investment into aviation, improve infrastructure and operations, and reduce the financial burden of managing public airports.

title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
summary: Funso Doherty says Peter Obi retains strong support in Lagos and could repeat his 2023 result. His remarks followed an attack that disrupted an NDC town hall.
body:
Funso Doherty, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Lagos, says Peter Obi retains the support needed to repeat his 2023 performance in the state. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Doherty rejected the suggestion that Obi’s move from the Labour Party to the NDC would weaken his appeal, arguing that voters are drawn to his political outlook rather than his party label.

Doherty said Obi’s reception remained strong and warned that politicians who dismissed his influence could misjudge the public mood. He pointed to the response of NDC supporters during an attack on the party’s town hall meeting as evidence that the enthusiasm seen during Obi’s 2023 campaign had not faded.

The meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, was disrupted before Obi and other party figures arrived.
